Priya (Eng): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: customers asked for clearer behavior when APAC capacity runs low. Can leadership confirm what happens for Hosted vs Dedicated?
Hannah (Product): Short answer: Dedicated pools can be provisioned with "reserved_nodes" to avoid fallbacks. Hosted will use cross-region routing when local free capacity is exhausted.
Omar (Infra): Technical detail: we have two fallback layers: 1) burst from warm pool (if configured), 2) cross-region routing. Burst is time-limited and subject to global quota.
Priya (Eng): Example policy we test with customers:
```
autoscaler_policy:
  warm_pool: 4
  burst:
    multiplier: 2
    duration_s: 180
  fallback:
    enabled: true
    prefer: regional
```
Omar (Infra): Important: for Dedicated with reserved_nodes > 0, fallback_cross_region is disabled until reserved+burst are drained. For Hosted, prefer regional means nearest region, then global.
Hannah (Product): Customer-facing FAQ points I'll draft: (1) expected latency impact when routed cross-region (~80-150ms median), (2) how to buy reserved capacity, (3) how to opt into warm pool for pilot.
Zoe (CTO): Action items: (A) Omar assemble short routing/SLA doc and add a diagram (ETA Thu), (B) Hannah populate pilot-customer list and mark Dedicated/private needs (ETA Tue EOD), (C) Priya prepare a small test checklist for pilot performance runs (ETA Wed).
sync-bot: Slides + recording uploaded: https://redwood.slack-recordings/1849999999 :page_with_curl:

Omar (Infra): I'll also wire up two dashboard metrics: apac_free_gpus, apac_fallback_events. Will PR panels and alerts by Wed morning.
Hannah (Product): If sales have urgent APAC private requests drop them in the pilot sheet; we'll triage for earliest onboarding.
Zoe (CTO): Good progress. Keep execs updated if procurement moves faster so we can expand pilot scope.
Priya (Eng): Closing thread, will post updates into #eng-infra RFC when docs land.
